set.typical_award_size: State density bonus and incentives implemented in NCZO Article 16 (Housing Element program HE-M update completed) and Coastal Zoning Ordinance Section 8175-6. Residential High Density (RHD) zone: seven parcels (four in the El Rio/Del Norte Area Plan within Oxnard's sphere of influence, two in the Existing Community of Santa Susana, one in the Piru Area Plan) allow 20 to 22 units per acre (before state density bonus) by ministerial RHD Zoning Clearance with no hearing; standards updated September 16, 2025 (program HE-H, NCZO Section 8109-1.3). Each RHD project must choose 20% lower income, 10% very low income, 5% extremely low income, or 30% lower income through alternative compliance (land donation or acquisition assistance to an eligible organization in a same-or-higher resource area of unincorporated Ventura County, or a proposal of equivalent action under Gov. Code 65850(g)). Piru expansion area projects must keep 10.5% of units affordable to low income households (not shown on the RHD page).

set.typical_award_size: State density bonus with local add-ons. Small and underutilized parcel incentives (Art. 7, Ord. 1568-NS): 100% affordable projects (all units except a manager unit for extremely low, very low or low income households, under recorded agreement) at a minimum 20 units per net acre on an existing parcel under 1/2 acre (alone or combined with contiguous parcels) or a Housing Element underutilized site may request any two extra incentives beyond density bonus incentives. Lot consolidation (Art. 8, Ord. 1734-NS, effective January 10, 2025): projects merging lots get a pre-application with no Planning Division fees, waivers of listed Mixed-Use standards (14-foot ground floor plate, 60-foot retail depth, third floor setback, 3% public exterior space), modified setbacks and height steps, reduced courtyard standards, and 65915(d)(2) regulatory incentives even without a density bonus.
set.affordability_requirement: Density bonus per Gov. Code 65915 with 55-year rental covenants; Article 7 incentives require 100% of units affordable to extremely low, very low or low income households; lot consolidation incentives on Housing Element sites require the inventory affordability, and on MU, MUOZ or R-3 sites outside the inventory require 20% of rental units for lower income or 20% of ownership units for moderate income households.
